newsitem.title: USA: Clinton "satisfied" with two choices for FED.
newsitem.headline: Clinton "satisfied" with two choices for FED.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is "satisfied" with two names submitted to him to fill current vacancies on the Federal Reserve Board and has asked that background checks be made, the White House said on Thursday.
White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry, while refusing to identify the two individuals, said the names were reviewed by Clinton and that "he's satisfied with the recommendations that came to him."
McCurry said that no final decision would be made until background checks were completed on both individuals. He said such investigations "can take several weeks, generally."
There currently are two vacancies on the board, following the departures of Laurence Lindsey and Janet Yellen, who now serves as head of the president's Council of Economic Advisers.

McCurry said he was commenting on the situation because there had been an erroneous news report on Wednesday that said Clinton was dissatisfied with the names submitted to him and had asked for additional choices.
